detail.longDescription: I'm cleaning up a dataset and some of the values are disjointed. It looks kind of like this: every city is in it's own row, and the columns show population. I want to merge A old and A new column values, without touching B. I don't know the row index that A old and A new are in, just the names. So I need to identify the rows through a conditional on the value of column name , and then adjust the value for each entry. Also, the entries might be numbers written as strings, or even left blank instead of zero. name 2000 2001 2002 2003 A old 3 2 0 0 A new 0 2 1 B 5 6 7 8 And desired result is: name 2000 2001 2002 2003 A old 3 2 0 0 A new 3 2 2 1 B 5 6 7 8 So far I have tried this: for k in range(2000,2004): df.loc[df['name']=="A new",str(k)]=df.loc[df['name']=="A new"][str(k)].replace('',0).astype(int)+df.loc[df['name']=="A old"][str(k)].replace('',0).astype(int) But this gives the result: name 2000 2001 2002 2003 A old 3 2 0 0 A new NaN NaN NaN NaN B 5 6 7 8 Any advice appreciated.
